title: Give the paseo wait a deadline so a hung wait cannot starve the heartbeat
action: Red first (bugfix): in the tests module of herding/run.rs, beside wait_for_round_paseo_timeout_keeps_the_run_alive and reusing FakePaseoCli and FakeWaitSource, add a test named wait_for_round_paseo_hung_wait_falls_back_to_inspect_and_keeps_a_running_agent_alive: FakeWaitSource with an empty queue (poll returns None forever, a wait that never returns), FakePaseoCli whose inspect returns {"Status":"running"}, idle_timeout_secs 120, ceiling 3600, a clock that advances 1000 ms per tick, and result-1.json written at tick 400. Run it on the current code and record that it ends TimedOutIdle instead of ResultReady. Then fix wait_for_round_paseo_driven (per 917fa9e4): remember the injected-clock time and the timeout_secs each time the wait is armed (both arm sites: the post-spawn arm and the re-arm block); in the branch that polls an active wait, when poll returns None and the current time is at or past armed_at + (armed timeout + 30 s), cancel the wait through the guard, set wait_active false, set in_error_fallback true and clear last_inspect_ms so the existing fallback branch inspects on the next tick. Make the 30 s grace one named const. The fallback branch already refreshes the heartbeat on a running inspect and allows a re-arm; do not duplicate it. The new test then reaches ResultReady, asserts cancel_count grew past the guard's final cancel and that more than one wait was armed. Every existing wait_for_round_paseo_ test stays green unchanged. No code comments of any kind (repo rule no_code_comments).

truths: A paseo wait that never returns no longer ends a running agent's job as timed_out_idle: after the wait deadline bee inspects, sees running, refreshes the heartbeat and re-arms
The new test fails on the old code with TimedOutIdle and passes on the fix with ResultReady
Every existing wait_for_round_paseo_ test passes unchanged
